message: Operation 'getTtm' has semantic quality issues: vague_summary, vague_description, missing_context, poor_ai_interpretability. Original summary is too technical and unclear. Description is extremely verbose, implementation-focused, and difficult for AI agents to parse. Reorganized to explain the core purpose (TTM calculation), key inputs (fiscal period, as_of date), supported filing types, required parameter matching, response content, and error conditions in a more digestible format.

data.current_description: Four fiscal quarters ending at the explicit fiscal_year and fiscal_quarter. Date as_of selects filed <= as_of; datetime as_of with an explicit offset selects accepted <= as_of. Fiscal periods require unique eligible filing metadata. Adjacent anchored period ends must be 2, 3 or 4 calendar months apart; the first and last of the four window ends, and the Q1 and Q4 ends of any fiscal year used to derive Q4, must be 8, 9 or 10 calendar months apart. Any other spacing is unavailable (422). Only 10-Q, 10-Q/A, 10-K and 10-K/A filings participate. Exact tag, taxonomy, unit, segments and coreg must agree. Omitted selectors must resolve to one series. Select the greatest (filed date, acceptance instant, accession) per period and duration; missing acceptance sorts first. Use discrete duration_quarters=1 facts, never cumulative YTD. Prefer reported Q4; otherwise subtract Q1, Q2 and Q3 from FY. Every quarter lists every contributing source, ordered FY then Q1 through Q3 for derived Q4. Identical inputs and source data produce byte-identical successful JSON. Malformed parameters return invalid_request; ambiguous selections return conflict; unavailable combinations return unprocessable. Scans exceeding 5000 eligible filings or 50000 matching facts return unprocessable, never a partial value.
data.description_suggestion: Calculates a trailing-twelve-month (TTM) financial metric by aggregating four consecutive fiscal quarters ending at the specified fiscal_year and fiscal_quarter. Supports point-in-time queries using as_of (date or datetime with offset) to select filings by filing or acceptance date. Only includes 10-Q, 10-Q/A, 10-K, and 10-K/A filings. Requires exact matches for tag, taxonomy, unit, segments, and coreg. Returns a TtmResponse containing the TTM value, component quarters, and source filing details. Validates fiscal quarter spacing (2-4 months between adjacent quarters, 8-10 months between first/last and fiscal year boundaries). Returns 422 for invalid spacing, 409 for ambiguous selections, or 422 for scans exceeding 5000 filings or 50000 facts.
data.reasoning: Original summary is too technical and unclear. Description is extremely verbose, implementation-focused, and difficult for AI agents to parse. Reorganized to explain the core purpose (TTM calculation), key inputs (fiscal period, as_of date), supported filing types, required parameter matching, response content, and error conditions in a more digestible format.

data.current_summary: Ticker and CIK mappings as of a date
data.current_description: Supply exactly one of ticker or cik. Returns every mapping in effect on as_of (valid_from <= as_of < valid_to; a null valid_to is open), each with its exchange, validity window, source and point_in_time. A ticker that maps to several CIKs on the date returns every candidate; none is picked. Mapping history starts at the first security master snapshot, so an as_of before it returns an empty data array. Name-only records are not served. Results are ordered by (cik, ticker, company_name, valid_from, source); the cursor binds the filter and the effective as_of.
data.description_suggestion: Retrieves ticker and CIK identifier mappings as of a specified date. Requires exactly one of ticker or cik as input. Returns all mappings valid on the as_of date (where valid_from <= as_of < valid_to; null valid_to indicates open-ended validity). Each mapping includes exchange, validity window, source, and point-in-time indicator. If a ticker maps to multiple CIKs on the specified date, all candidates are returned without disambiguation. Results are ordered by (cik, ticker, company_name, valid_from, source) with cursor-based pagination. Note: Mapping history begins at the first security master snapshot, so as_of dates before that return an empty data array. Name-only records are excluded.
